briefs.polymarket-7121567: The question settles on the Binance BTC/USDT 1-minute candle closing at 12:00 ET on 2026-11-24 (16:00-16:01 UTC); it needs a close above 58,000, and exactly 58,000 is No. Binance's ticker read about 63,820 on 2026-11-19 around 10:15 UTC (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/ticker/price?symbol=BTCUSDT), about 10% above the threshold. The 2026-11-18 daily close was 63,068.22 (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=1d&limit=3), and price has fallen about 23% from 83,028 on 2026-10-20. The 30-day standard deviation of daily log returns is about 0.023, so the roughly 126 hours left give a one-sigma move near 5.4%, and the gap is about 1.9 sigma. The reference class is every 5-day window of Binance daily closes since 2017-08-17: 3,112 of 3,377 (92.2%) stayed above 0.9089 times the starting close, 96.8% over the last 4 years and 96.3% over the last 2 years. This is unconditional and uses daily closes as a proxy for the settling minute. Different this time: US spot bitcoin ETFs had $2.58 billion of net outflows from Nov 2 to Nov 17, about 87% from IBIT (https://news.bitcoin.com/bitcoin-etf/bitcoin-etfs-lose-2-58b-in-november-with-blackrock-driving-the-exit/, 2026-11-18), and bitcoin slid under 70,000 on Nov 13 with no single trigger (https://investinglive.com/cryptocurrency/bitcoin-dipped-under-70k-first-time-since-august/). No scheduled macro event falls before resolution: the FOMC is on Dec 8-9 and November CPI on Dec 10 (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-december.htm, https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm). Unknowns include ETF flows after Nov 17, any Nov 18-19 news, and a roughly 46 USD gap between the Binance trade page and the API ticker. A further decline of about 9-10% before Nov 24, for example from continued outflows or a liquidation cascade, would change the answer.
briefs.polymarket-7029662: The question resolves Yes if IMF PortWatch daily total transit calls (container, dry bulk, ro-ro, general cargo, tanker) for Bab el-Mandeb reach 30 or more on any single date from 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22. The PortWatch resolution page returned no data in the digest's pass, so the 16-22 November series is unknown. The PortWatch daily layer (https://services9.arcgis.com/weJ1QsnbMYJlCHdG/arcgis/rest/services/Daily_Chokepoints_Data/FeatureServer/0) holds data to 2026-11-15, with totals for 9-15 November of 29, 25, 19, 24, 28, 20 and 34. Days at 30 or more were 11 of 31 in August, 8 of 30 in September, 12 of 31 in October and 4 of 15 in 1-15 November 2026. Base rate: all 1,795 seven-day windows from 2019 to 2023-11 reached 30, 1,034 of 1,044 (99.0%) since January 2024, and 82 of 91 (90.1%) over the trailing 90 days. In the same calendar week the maximum was 39 in 2024 and 47 in 2025. Different this time: JMIC recorded about 22 commercial transits a day on 12-14 November (https://www.shipuniverse.com/?p=27890) and the threat is rated substantial with no recent incidents (https://www.lloydslistintelligence.com/resources/blog/red-sea-brief---12-november-2026). Other trackers differ in method, such as Gulf News at about 34 a day on 1-4 November and Lloyd's List with 1,363 October transits. Yemeni government-aligned forces withdrew from positions near the strait on 15 November and Houthi media said the Houthis took control of the area (https://newsonair.gov.in/houthis-take-control-of-bab-al-mandab-strait-area-following-withdrawal-of-yemeni-government-forces/, 2026-11-16). That could raise pressure on shipping, but no attack was confirmed for the window. A week with no day at 30 or more, perhaps after a new attack or a lasting dip in traffic, or a publication problem on PortWatch would make this No.
briefs.polymarket-2915400: The initiative 'For a restriction on fireworks' is on the 29 November 2026 federal ballot and needs both a popular majority and a majority of cantons (half-cantons count as half). The Federal Council and Parliament recommend No, saying it goes too far because cantons and municipalities can already restrict fireworks (https://www.admin.ch/feuerwerksinitiative); a cross-party No campaign with SVP, FDP and Mitte launched on 6 October (https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/verbot-von-boellern-nein-kampagne-gegen-feuerwerksinitiative-lanciert). The National Council rejected the indirect counter-proposal, so the initiative is on the ballot alone (https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/verbot-von-boellern-feuerwerksinitiative-kommt-ohne-gegenvorschlag-vors-volk, 2026-06-26). The first SRG/gfs.bern wave (fieldwork 5-18 October, 14,874 voters) found 69% in favour (https://www.srf.ch/news/erste-srg-umfrage-ja-vorteil-fuer-feuerwerksinitiative-meinungen-fast-gemacht, 2026-10-23). The second wave, published 2026-11-18, says the initiative would have been clearly approved on 7 November, but the percentages were not read (https://www.gfsbern.ch/en/news/2nd-srg-survey-on-the-federal-votes-of-29-november-2026). The final YouGov barometer (fieldwork 2-16 November, 3,013 voters) had 59% yes, 36% no and 5% undecided (https://yougov.com/de-de/artikel/56001-fairness-initiative-bricht-ein-kriegsmaterialgesetz-bleibt-offen-wie-will-die-schweiz-am-29-november-abstimmen). Base rate: only about 9-11% of federal initiatives pass (22 of 192 from 1893 to 2014, 17 of 182 from 1970 to 2020), but those counts come from secondary sources and do not condition on polls this strong. Initiatives typically lose support during the campaign, which the fall from 69% to 59% across pollsters may reflect. The cantonal majority is unpolled, and rural German-speaking cantons are the main risk. A narrower final margin, or a gfs second wave showing a yes lead below about 55%, would lower the chance of passing.
briefs.manifold-NP9CqulZcA: The question asks whether Ritchie Torres will be the next governor of New York, resolving on certified results from the State Board of Elections, whose pages returned HTTP 403, so the exact rule was not confirmed. Kathy Hochul won the 2026-11-03 general election over Republican Bruce Blakeman; the AP called it as polls closed at 9 p.m. (https://www.wamc.org/2026-11-03/kathy-hochul-re-elected-new-york-governor-defeats-bruce-blakeman, https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/11/hochul-cruises-reelection/417017/). Preliminary results at 92% reporting were 60% to 40%, and a margin of about 20 points will not flip on canvass. Torres told MSNBC on 2025-07-02 that he was 'unlikely to run for governor' (https://www.bxtimes.com/torres-wont-run-for-governor/, 2025-07-03) and endorsed Hochul on 2025-08-19 (https://bronx.news12.com/news-12-exclusive-rep-ritchie-torres-endorses-kathy-hochul-for-governor). He is not on the 2026 gubernatorial ballot, and his House race in NY-15 is a separate contest. A search-result summary of the elections calendar gives county canvass by 2026-11-28 and state certification by 2026-12-15, after the 2026-11-29 date in the digest. No base rate was counted, since the question needs someone not on the ballot to become governor. The only residual uncertainty is how 'next governor' is read, as the 2026 winner or the person taking office on 2027-01-01, and under either reading the person is Hochul. Only a resolution quirk, or a surprise vacancy and succession involving Torres, would change the answer, and nothing in the digest suggests either.
